1 Introduction
(To the Material Science and Computational Modelling (AI & Modelling))
Welcome, to the research documentation page on material science and such applications or investigations using artificial intelligence, for the lack of better work downgrading current infrastructures to, and computational simulation, without restriction to simple binary simulation itself. Our purpose in such research is then fairly simple to state. More specifically, what we want includes:

Investigation of the foundational concepts, constructs, models, realization, assumption, oracle specification, truncated regions, meaning, and so on when in consideration of physics, to subject as specific of materials and their structural consequences.
We study the intrinsic image and realization of different models as such in material science, from which we identify of the structural error, region of fallacy, failure modes and so on that instead of entangle the system in a network of patchwork, we diagnose specific pattern and junctions where analysis on multi-angle model cohesion can be achieved. Within such, perhaps proposal for new models or a unified one can be attained.
We study the close problem between theoretical-practical gap of material science on paper and of its instantiation, for also computer simulation models.
Within it, we study simulation theory in close quarter to material science, the simulated problem on the inability to capture many-body physics without using upper-layer zoom-out measure (statistics and quantum mechanics are admission of such that the details are either too complex, or too unknown to be grounded specifically). The gap is then also between described construction and admitted structures, in which we are to realize on the method to simulate a structure more than just numerical computation, and furthermore on the disadvantage, compartment removal in such method of simulating under constraints.
Using AI, or rather, applying AI toward specific structural purposes, we probe the usage of AI-like system for the lack of analysis thereof, to see their applications, inherited or extracted features, the fitting patterns that they design or extrapolated, and furthermore the inherent limitation they carry. Ever more specifically, if we are to treat AI system as tangible for realization of material science structure, we ought to also realize what they capture and how the semantic dynamic structure is moved in-between of the AI substrates.

With such, our goal is rather large. The first section perhaps would cover the more basic of material science, as a survey into within itself of the field, and further more if time and resource is allowed. Nevertheless, within such a long plan, we are to fill it with not buzzword but actual concepts. For the lack of word and the abundance thereof being superficial teleology, we are to say the words toward what they are worth.
This is inherited, or born out of participation of the Computational Material Science Laboratory. Following up of such, I thank for their guidances thereof.

Before studying anything about material science, we might as well be familiarized of the concept, and the historiography on what material can be constituted of. Surprisingly, or rather the unsurprising thereof, is that such concept has been presented in a very long time, ever since the old age of the Roman Empire, and further down the path.
In the age of Ancient Rome, two books, the De Architectura by Vitruvius and naturalis Historia by Pliny the Elder, gives us the portrait of the material science, or the knowledge in specificity about materials, in Rome at the beginning of the Empire. In most of the case studies, it is in the making of four case studies: concretes, coatings, amorphous materials, and colloidal crystals, to describe them in the modern corpora of words.
The word science itself comes from the Latin scientia, for which to mean “knowledge”, and then, to find the material science of the past, it is natural to respond it toward the “knowledge of materials”. Interestingly, such knowledge as seen of the use cases, often accompanied us within which our life interacts of it. Such is why, the question of material science in those times are not rather fundamental, but before the requirement of the body of studies, one ask:

Though, it does not bring about much in short or medium-term of meaningful actions, such is also why typically, the equation of which we draw about material science would not include that (however, we do note such are rather useful, and would be nice to get).

The part is rather interesting - if such is mixed with lime and rubble, it hardens as well under water as in ordinary buildings. Under their civilization perspective, such is rather interesting, because it is basically a type of constructive medium in which can be used to build, of course, building or any form of structures. Marcus Vitruvius Pollio lived in the 1st century BC. He was a Roman architect and engineer, best known as the author of the “De Architectura” [5]. Gaius Plinius Secundus, known as Pliny the Elder, died on 25 August, 79 AD during the eruption of Mount Vesusius. He was a Roman naturalist as well as naval commander of the Roman Empire. He wrote an encyclopaedic work, the “Naturalis Historia” [6]. These two books give us a portrait of knowledge in Rome, at the beginning of the Empire, and deserve a longer study. For instance, the “Naturalis Historia” contains several detailed descriptions of metals, pigments and precious stones.



There is a species of sand which, naturally, possesses extraordinary qualities. It is found about Baiae and the territory in the neighbourhood of Mount Vesuvius; if mixed with lime and rubble, it hardens as well under water as in ordinary buildings. This seems to arise from the hotness of the earth under these mountains and the abundance of springs under their bases. (Vitruvius, translated)

But he notes that in Tuscany, where there are several hot springs too, “we do not there find a powder, which, for the same reason, would harden under water … All lands do not possess similar qualities; nor is stone universally found. 2.2 The modern history of material science
Due of history, material science emerged full-fledged in the USA, some time in the early 1950s. However, the period before it stems much of the context into which the current structure of material science is of present. And a fairly dirty history one can get from it. Per Mody and Martin (2020) for example, such is rather famously taken of a complicated history at large.
Material science stems from, or rather inherited of the settled practices toward what metallurgy is, which have been in existence for a rather long period of time. During the 18th-19th centuries of the enlightenment, knowledge about materials, specifically if we are to host an operational form on what constitutes a material. Traditionally, material in consideration is this solid, but the wider range can be pointed to any form of matter in hosting all state of matters, or now so we speak. In such it also includes, obviously, foundational matters of biological one, so to speak.
There, we gradually gain the empirical ground on metallurgy, chemistry, mechanical engineering, and industrial manufacturing. Per Cahn (2001) and Eliade (1956), of which gives many craft knowledge and scientific investigation of the substrate itself, but not by much being the field of material science. That is because, there exists no middle ground on theories at that focal point, so much so material investigations were solely considered as to be the instantiation of the physical theories and thereof, most often the very general foundational theory of physics. Many would say that material science did not exist before 1950s, and such would be hard to refute.

2.2.1 Cold War reorganization
During the Cold War, the entire field was considered and rather transformed into being of existence, taking on specific pipelines, and body of theories starting from source materials into the actual objects.

Through the mid-1950s, Cold War competition focused principally on nuclear weapons development as the United States and the Soviet Union raced to amass larger and larger arsenals. But within the logic of nuclear deterrence, the delivery systems for nuclear weapons mattered just as much as the weapons themselves. A nation with powerful enough rockets could deliver a nuclear warhead to any spot it chose on the globe. The Soviet launch of the world’s first artificial satellite, Sputnik, on October 4, 1957, therefore represented a shift. The aluminium sphere’s radio blips were not as consequential as the demonstration of rocketry powerful enough to launch a satellite into space—or deliver a nuclear warhead. Some nuclear capabilities would still be based on nuclear-armed aircraft, and later submarines, but an increasing proportion of the nuclear powers’ arsenals would sit on the tip of sophisticated rockets, ready to race toward their targets at a moment’s notice.

Born out of metallurgy (for details, see Cahn (2001)), material science was considered a superdiscipline, as it hinges on very much the entire landscape of science at large of the moment, stretching of all apparatus, theories of all scales, and thus encompassing an unusual interdisciplinary environment condition. The reorganization of material science defines the field by modern standard as to be certainly a pluralism of details

David Turnbull, in his illuminating Commentary on the Emergence and Evolution of “Materials Science” (Turnbull 1983), defined materials science “broadly” as “the characterisation, understanding, and control of the structure of matter at the ultramolecular level and the relating of this structure to properties (mechanical. magnetic, electrical, etc.). That is, it is ‘Ultramolecular Science’.”

or, in one way or another in COSMAT Report of 1974, as

[…] concerned with the generation and application of knowledge relating the composition, structure, and processing of materials to their properties and uses.

During the mid-1950s, there existed at that time, two traditions that would rather unable to talk with one another. First, was the industrial research sector, exemplified by Bell Laboratories, and so forth, but not limited to of legacy, per individual empiricisms without foundation of the Bessemer process (1856), the Siemens-Martin open-hearth furnace (1860s), the Hall-Héroult aluminium process (1886). This only comes back and forth toward temporal inversion - technology precedes theory, theory then rationalizes technology - will soon be observed again pre-formation as such. Bell Lab functioned as more of an industrial research system rather than the typical conventional laboratory that you would see, operating inside a vertically integrated telecommunications monopoly that treated discovery as infrastructure, perhaps more than just some patents. The purposes were not to chase products or market timing but to solve fundamental problems that would stabilize and extend a national communication network, which in turns the monopoly money being reinvested into more foundational problem. Such created of itself an insulating internal culture that permits Bell Laboratory to get the transistor (1947), information theory (1948), laser partly of itself, and so on, and shield them from having to chase external peer review or annual grant cycles, nor commercially relevant products’ formation. As such, we say, that science precedes the commercial utilization.
The other sector was the academic disciplinary science, which is the traditional one where metallurgy grown out of mining engineering curricula were positioned. Working on rather a practical and empirical side, solid-state physics, ceramic engineering, polymer chemistry, and so on, they are settled, at the time, to live in separate buildings, separate departments, using only foundational physics as justification, separate conferences, trained in separate PhD programs, and all of the above. These communities were intellectually productive but siloed, and each was, in Paul Forman’s phrasing, partly insulated from the guiding hand of physics — meaning that engineering-oriented metallurgists and ceramicists were not strongly connected to the theoretical advances in quantum mechanics and statistical mechanics that, in retrospect, were directly relevant to their problems, but without a different eye on the paper sheet.
One example can be filled deliberately, is within the organic and inorganic chemistry of which came into an ever-increasing conflict throughout the nineteenth century, and “indeed as recently as 1969 an eminent British chemist was quoted as asserting that ‘inorganic chemistry is a ridiculous field’”. Both sides are rather deliberately correct on their own, and far wrong on the others, with understanding of what was going on internally of the synthesis of compounds and compositional analysis, specifically on carbon-based structures of organic chemistry and the possibility of the lack thereof, from the inorganic one, remained bedevilled by a number of confusions, “for instance, between gaseous atoms and molecules, the absence of such concepts as stereochemistry and isomerism”. Even right now, the scale problem is particularly absent, to say that chemistry itself did not organize the field within scales and frames in which operatives from foundational primitives are sufficed to characterize which phenomena belong to where, and of what precursor that gives rise to such process, either multi-layer leaks on local-global interaction or not. Unsurprisingly, during such period, there was no agreed atomic theory, and even uncertainty about atomic weights, especially the inorganic elements. Even by now, such problem remains in practice of interaction, as for while there exists the standard model, interactions and dynamics of nuclear physics largely depends on a rather unpleasant proliferation of concepts and pluralism of patchwork models, that is used to understand nucleic interactions and productions.

Another thing to note, lies rather in the physics itself. During the earlier development of metallurgy, during the 1920s, for example with Frenkel’s paper (Frenkel 1926), established what was then known as the plastic deformation paradox. Within such, Frenkel estimated the stress required to slide one atomic plane over another in a perfect lattice and thus gave \[
\tau_{ideal}\approx \frac{G}{2\pi}
\] where \(G\) is the shear modulus. For typical metals, this gives \(\tau_{ideal}\sim 10^{-1}G\), however, experimental yield stresses were typically \(\tau_{exp}\sim 10^{-4}G\). Thus, there exists the discrepancy of the theory itself, and what the experiment gives. By the late 1920s, the discrepancy between theory and experiment of such was widely recognized in crystal physics and metallurgy, for which it is rather troubling because the predictions stemming from such rather suspiciously stable theory can be catastrophically wrong. Such stemmed the efforts made by which is the recognition for dislocation theory, for the specifically jointed tension effort by (Orowan 1934), (Polanyi 1934), then (Taylor 1934) and empirically confirmed of the conjecture by (Hirsch et al. 2006). where one posits that plastic deformation occurs through line defects than uniform sliding of entire planes. Essentially turning them to local (relatively) events. More specifically, it reframes the entire stress deformation as

A dislocation is a linear crystallographic defect whose motion allows atoms to slide at low stress.

And then, such was used throughout for the theory itself. However, even within such, inconsistency remains between continuum plasticity theory and microscopic dislocation dynamics. This is partially because the interpretation apparatus considered of those structures and theories are entangled, for one is concerned with smooth fields condensation for deformation on continuum, and one defines them via discrete avalanche-like events. The dislocation theory itself carries its fair share of paradox, for example, the paradox of strength and ductility, per (Valiev et al. 2002), for which refers to the difficulty of achieving both high strength and high ductility in materials. A rather more catastrophic one is the Frank-Read source, for which is the mechanism for generation of multiple dislocation in well-spaced slip planes in crystalline structures, under deformation. Even with a recent 2024 papers, they only demonstrated the aspect of empirical deformation under multiplication dislocations. The issue remains that a perfect crystal, initially contains very few dislocations, yet during plastic deformation gives huge density of such. So, where do dislocations come from? Such require jumping outside the framework itself, of which then arguably confusing as to question its own ontology. Which might as well never work. Such also brings about the recent (quite so?) discovery of the severe plastic deformation paradox, which can be seen in (Valiev 2003), and persisted ever since.

Within such systematic decoupling, of the academic field and the industry, the alignment of interests and system default, it is rather not surprising to see the developments failed in a way or another. While one party goes on one way, the other emphasizes another aspect of such. While Bell Laboratory, and many powerhouses of industrial research purposes were given freedom and exploratory merits that feed back to the grinding halt of the private proprietary claims, the other side is largely institutional, fragmented, argued of each other while given no quarter for actual communication and coherence of analysis. Academic tradition was often considered building knowledge for its own sake, organized around disciplinary identity and themed discussion, not allowing for anything else than internal peer recognition and specialties of identity, while the industrial one forgone any kind of theoretical scientific notion, in pursuits of empirical but successful products. The only problem at that point, is the lack of communication between the two, and the internal problem that crippled dialogues from within.
When Sputnik launched in October 4th, 1957, the dialogue switched dramatically into overdrive. It is by then observed of those under administration roles to see of such dilemma, insufficient understanding of materials represented of the 1950s directly to a strategic shortcoming. We do have novel material per se, we do have many wonderful architectural designs. But we do not have a coherent theory, a stable framework, or any form of practical identification or practical theory of sort. Materials Advisory Board’s 1967 report outlined some of such - characterization of material is a bottleneck (and may right now still be within its large complex structures without structural conditions), material construction identification is also a problem, effective theory and usage of materials of the time is mostly unknown, and perhaps furthermore, the practical-theoretical gap is strictly hierarchical officially - where practical knowledges serve to be the second-order of what of the constitution. Utilizing such, the response was framed by specific ideological commitment, of which (Mody and Martin 2020) specified and identified as decisive - many scientists, most specifically American-Western scientists of physics in general, valorized ‘pure science’ and sought to distant themselves from such practical outcomes of their work. Physicists, those of whom are apart from the realization in the physical world, convinced the administrators and generals that engineering is not there sufficient anymore, such is to say paving way for the physics to be of higher-order, and metallurgy, production science, plastic science, to be simply not capable. This, is rather a self-serving framing for physicists - it positioned physics as master science that would redeem the backward engineering fields. That said, the most productive materials research of the preceding decades had come not from physicists imposing their framework on metallurgists and those manufacturing of their own practical devices, but to get the environment similar to Bell Labs, where there exists no clear hierarchy rather than the instantiation thereof, of the distance to be none, that a singular problem can be argued from both side and work on the same range, without the relationship being hierarchical. Such explains of the interdisciplinary failures, the failure of cumulative pluralism, internal disciplinary acceptance of which is rather counterproductive on its own, and the rigidity of expression and backward incompatibility the field inherited parts of.


2.2.2 To the present day
This section is here for now only to serve as the self-serving opening to the next sections. That is rather trivial, because we aim toward clarify the problems inherent of the current structures. Those, and of the fragmentation we would be seeing, came from a long line of slow decays, most often than not the fault of, or not, of the field itself.

From what we have listed after which the Cold War happened, it is easy to get yourself lost in the land of which material science bases itself in. The history has not been so kind to the precursors of material science on itself. During much course of histories, material science has been staying in the lane of intriguing but disfranchising field of accumulated research, specifically targeting certain parts of the material landscape. The definition of material, even up to present, is largely incoherent thereof, that it would be difficult to classify of what to be material, as some may even argue that water is a type of material, or it can be a solvent, or it can be a neutral medium. The Hylomorphism in Aristotle’s Theory


The notion is toward what are essentially compositional thought, for Aristotle of his general ideas. Aristotle defines matter as to be ‘out of which’ something is made. For example, letters are the matter of syllables. Thus, matter is a relative term: an object counts as matter relative to something else. Clay is matter relative to a brick because a brick is made of clay, at that specific point, whereas bricks are matter relative to a brick house. Change is analyzed as a material transformation, for where matter is what undergoes a change of form. Due of history, before Lavoisier made his progresses, Georg Ernst Stahl as the German chemist of the old day, proposed what we now call as phlogiston, of which being the intangible substance released from fermentation, combustion and relevant processes of the kind (note that this is deliberately arbitrary). Thus, every object or matter in consideration of a specific interaction process, forgoing the question of matter-property but to treat it as plain object of distinguishment, to be of specific amount of \(\mathrm{Ph}(A)\) for object class \(A\). During combustion, then for example, phlogiston was thought to be expelled into air, resulting in a dephlogisticated residue, such as wood ash (see more in here). On the surface, it seems probable, as during such transformation process, there exists the residue of which we can see of the transformation being \(A\to B+ C\), where \(C\) is the ash and \(B\) is the product (we are doing process schema here). The question of how \(C\) were there, in the first place, is the Aristotle question asked of the lower level, and here Stahl predicated it with phlogiston. How Lavoisier disproved it? Well, not by operating within the framework itself, because the framework is sound in its question of deliverance - there must be something that give rise to such combustion residue - the residue does not really look like \(A\), nor it is similar to what \(B\) produced. So there are external factors, or, in this case, another internal factor of itself in the subject that would only be released by interaction in the kind of combustion (here, is the interaction picture). Instead, Lavoisier attempted the experiment to show that combustion involves oxygen that transform the subject itself. This targets a rather simple case - metal rust, where the object actually during the process increases of volume instead of reducing, of which supposedly reducing in phlogiston during the process set up a kind of internal conservation law within itself - that phlogiston + matter would stay the same instead; which, evidently, is not the case. As of such, we have the following empirical refutation of which one made to disprove at such boundary.


Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier, the most prominent antiphlogistonist, believed that calcination produced a weight gain in metals because something in the air combined with the metal. He repeated the experiments of Priestley, interpreting the change in the lead calx as the loss of a gas into the air. This explanation solved the problem of weight gain experienced by metals when calcinated: Lavoisier reasoned that the same gas that a calcinated metal released had bonded to it when it was originally calcinated, and the weight of the gas had been added to the weight of the pure metal at that time. Lavoisier named this new gas “oxygen.” Although Lavoisier was never able to dissuade Priestley from believing in phlogiston, he did convince most other chemists of his day that the theory needed to be discarded. 4
4 Even then, we can see that not even Lavoisier can convince the phlogistonists such as Priestley himself. His experiment is rather sound, however despite popular beliefs and what to be considered of the narrative refutation. In one, he heated some calx of lead (mercuric oxide) in a closed container and found that the air released by the calx caused a candle to burn more vigorously and that a mouse placed in the container could breathe longer than when placed in normal air. Priestley called the air inside the container “dephlogisticated air”: He assumed that, by heating lead calx, he had removed phlogiston from normal air and caused it to be reabsorbed by the calx. In fact, rather than removing something from the air, Priestley had added to it when the heated mercuric oxide gave off oxygen. Without the knowledge nor the realization of the breaking case, one would have to see that the evidences inside, suggested phlogiston to be rather right.
The ontological baseline now shifted, where phlogiston is actually the substance air of which combine to give the effect a stable cause. The question again shifted toward, what is even air? How would air combines with the matter of metal to produce combustion? The layer is now clarified quite a bit, as for there must be something smaller that make up both the metal, and both the air, for them to interact and give rise to residue, albeit of the same mass for both as it is. It is also a rather early entry to the concept of entropy and energy transformation - if we are to have same mass, accumulated throughout air giving in to give rise to rust and so on, then during the process of burning, we lose the torch and of the fire soon fade. Then, what is transformed, and what was lost during that process? Such question would be answered later, or rather not, as the body of science already gave its way toward it, and we should not reinvent nor reinterpreting it, lest of the space available in the discourse such is this small section. That said, we now have the conservation law of Mass, where now mass of constituent, actually can be traced to specific interaction partners of the process, not merely attribute more to what there exists. Such is also again, a problem of which still surfaces as of the modern context - how do you characterize materials good enough to get that distinction, and should that be answered, many would be elucidated of the process. For now, the revolution points itself to the quality of which that can be qualified, for the first time in many decades of works.
Let us end the section by taking on the implications thereof for this linage of itself, and of the chemical revolution in its entirety. Namely, the technological ‘marvel’ thereof. For what to be seen from (American Chemical Society (ACS) n.d.a), (American Chemical Society (ACS), n.d.-b), (Flavell-While 2011), (Roebuck n.d. / c. 1746), (Encyclopaedia Britannica Editors, n.d.-d), (Encyclopaedia Britannica Editors, n.d.-b), (Encyclopaedia Britannica Editors, n.d.-a), and of (Encyclopaedia Britannica Editors, n.d.-c) for what history preserved of intentions and records, the Chemical Revolution indeed made the depth of how materials were to be defined, albeit with the same constraints we set above.

Klein & Lefèvre show that 18th-century chemists developed a new ontology of substances: they identified and categorized “pure chemical substances” by composition. For example, air was re-ontologized into oxygen, nitrogen, etc. Traditional “affinity tables” of the pre-1789 era (organizing substances by reaction affinities) gave way to Lavoisier’s Tableau de nomenclature chimique (1787), classifying substances by elemental makeup5.
5 Again, we note the lower-level commitment here as non-trivial. It will recur in later organization.
Much can be said of the later work, i.e. Dalton’s atomic theory to enhance such, and also to explain of what to be said from our analysis, to be of the following incursion. The atomic theory helped in the way of the forced hand of description, during which it proposed:

All matter is composed of extremely small indivisible particles called atoms.
Atoms, of a given element are identical in size, mass and other properties. Atoms of different elements differ in size, mass and other properties. Such is to say, we have the atomic species, or, elements.
Atoms cannot be subdivided, created or destroyed. That is, atoms of an element are not changed into atoms of a different element during chemical reaction.
Atoms of different elements combined in simple whole number ratios to form chemical compounds.
In chemical reactions, atoms are combined, separated or rearranged.
In a given compound, the relative number and kind of atoms are constant.

Supported by again, Lavoisier, alongside the set of empirical law on conservation of mass, the law of definite proportions, and law of constant composition, and, lastly, multiple proportions. What is said, however, is that the apparent contradiction of the grounding to shut down the lower-level constituent, has been settled. What to be lower than the atom itself is not in the question but delegated into impossibility - we simply cannot reach. In a sense, and of the period, such worked spectacularly within the domain where such grounding is applicable. History, however, writes itself. And so far, before we move on to diagnose the failure of such, we are set one account that by virtue of our currently knowledge only, would be contingent to the realization. The quark was being idle.
For industrial chemistry itself, the new chemistry indeed gained operational success, especially of large-scale chemical manufacturing process. The two often cited prospect arose to be as followed,

Sulphuric acid: John Roebuck’s lead-chamber process (1746) allowed bulk acid production. By lining wooden reaction chambers with lead, Roebuck’s method produced concentrated sulphuric acid at far lower cost. This massive supply of acid fuelled textiles, metallurgy and later fertilizers.
Soda ash: Nicolas Leblanc devised a process (patented 1791) to make soda from common salt and sulphuric acid. Leblanc’s method “turned soda production from nothingness to a major industry”. His 1791 patent was lauded as “very superior” in economy and purity. Mid-19th century production reached ~400,000 tons/year. These early chemical plants (sulphuric acid, soda) were among the first examples of the modern chemical industry.

At last, from 1780s, the shift has been to be foundational - where substances were identified, individuated, ordered per specification of certain dialect, and classed on the basis of their composition. What seemed to be mundane and non-trivial, by such effect, are now the central of studies in the search for the elemental substrates underlying typically can be said of almost everything that can be made of in nature. The ontological shift is now fair bit better - while the lower-level still retains the inherent grounding question, such is to say the layer worked far better than anticipated, one part no small of its simplification and enunciation for which materials are identified under empirical analysis isolated enough to trivialize complexity, as it is certainly one would not want his chainsaw to be reek of rust when he first began the journey into lumbering. In a sense, chemists started regarding matter, and materials thereof, as a set of chemically defined substances. The shift occurred in matter. The material does not.

3.2 Modern scientific theories on material sciences
It is rather undermining to start the section about what to be said of material science to be an elaboration from what industrial and chemical revolution are to be of. Almost arrogantly, we settled on the rhetoric that the history of material science of the modern time only starts here. What we have done in the 20th and 21st century would be in the same time bracket, and of which there are no ‘modern’ in the sense of what we usually claim, but the modern here had been there for more than two hundred years. And, under just the behest of what to come, I commit to that position. I simply posit the simple directive that under the very process of the 19th-20th-21st century of now, what we have been seeing and patching, is the patchwork of many, if not proliferation of pluralism in itself, to what as to be said of the same ground, with cartography stretched from not Europe but to the American Continent - just that we ought to mistake it for India.
About at the end of the Lavoisier-Dalton revolution onward, the artefact remains the two criteria of material sciences. What to be said to be incompatible, and of which to be said of not the same.






NoteCriterion CR.1.



A material/matter is identified by its composition - its elemental makeup and molecular structure. Two samples with the same composition are the same material, since their constituent parts are the same.








NoteCriterion CR.2.



A material/matter is identified by its functional behaviour in context - its response to processing, performance in utilization and application, and its participation to be configured in activation relation. Two samples with the same composition with different processing histories are different materials, if they perform differently.


This inherent contradiction lives within the mechanical revolution and chemical revolution practical consideration, and the principle of such to be said of the atomic constituent model itself. On one side, there is the insistence on Aristotle invariance, where the lower level is fundamental enough as to dissolve the dynamics, of which for when the matter itself is utilized 6, it would be the same material in all and of all. One the other side, there exists the functional invariance of the observable set - which is to say in plain language of the worker man as to be if it works, it works and if it is the same, expect us to bang for bucks the same way. Those two cannot live entirely of one another, without trespassing on themselves. These criteria conflict even in the simple case of graphite and diamond, and of which the cooled steel in rapid process or slow-cooling behaves different from one another of itself. If we are to believe that chemical revolution brings the grounding of two separated materials to be entirely same, yet somewhere they are different, one must ask: what are the properties we of which are missing of? And more importantly, if atoms cannot explain it of the atomic periodic table to be in the same position, will Aristotle return? The answer is yes.
6 And in a sense, becoming material, though that is another target to be distinguished, as always.
3.2.1 The failure of Dalton’s
What to be said as the failure of Dalton’s atomic theory (1808), is rather easy to unpack where it went wrong and what to be said of itself. Garnett (1996) and Bucat (1984) specified in a rather different details of the following information that we would be able to take apart from, which will be of relevant in later sections still.

Gas particles are evenly scattered in an enclosed space and there are empty space between particles.
Particles move slower in liquids and vibrate about fixed positions in solids.
Particles join together in simple consistent ratios when two different substances react to form a third substance.
Mass is conserved in these reactions.
The spacing between solid-solid, liquid-liquid and gas-gas particles is close to 1:1:10 (Andersson, 1990; de Vos and Verdonk, 1996).

Many years apart, the story often presented in the corpus of chemical science would be of the atomic theory since Dalton, and the current molecular kinetic theory, though much more antique in consideration against quantum chemistry, are actually closer than what we thought. The current molecular story only imported the higher resolution of the consequence of Dalton’s - such is where atoms would be still, the driving force, and their behaviours are explainable in the sense of which their connections, topology, reactions are derivable with precision of the rulesets to follow along, and it should always be that way. Or not, as we would find out. But for now, let us take apart each of them, one by one.

The form of Dalton’s
Suppose matter/material collapse into a singular topic of discussion about its origin. Then, The atomic model indicts that matter \(M\) has the composition from \(N(k)\), for \(N\in\mathcal{N}\) of the atomic species, i.e. the distinct set of elements altogether, \(k\) denoting the simple cardinality as a whole. Then, we posit that certain element of \(N_{1}\) and \(N_{2}\) are equal only if the properties attached to them are of the same quantitative evaluation, we call this \(\{p\}\). The first advantage of Dalton’s theory is that we can settle on the similarity up to a certain point, based on empirical observation of standardized quantity. The size, up to certain fixture of propositional evaluation, also is rather easier of the intuition. We can say that iron are much bigger/smaller than oxygen atom, to a given sense, and such would be verified by local experience alone, and would not need much explanation thereof - you can feel the bulk of iron, but not so much of oxygen, that is. Chemical reaction happens when sufficient condition are there to mix between \(N_{1}+N_{2}\). Now, the key point of Dalton is that \[
\frac{k_{1}}{k_{2}} = c\in \mathbb{Q}
\] of all whole number, for \(k_{1}\) the units of element of \(N_{1}\), and so on for \(k_{2}\). Discrete combinatorial units of each element in a stable structure, is the kinematic of interaction that they would be able to occur of. Thence, for a set of \(m\) chemical compounds, the following applies for all chemical reaction, \[
N_{1} + N_{2} + N_{3} + \dots + N_{m} = (\dots((N_{1} + N_{2}) + N_{3}) + \dots + N_{m} )
\] subjected to \[
\frac{k_{1}}{k_{2}} , \frac{k_{12}}{k_{3}}, \frac{k_{123}}{k_{4}}, \dots , \frac{k_{1\dots m-1}}{k_{m}} \in \mathbb{Q},
\] For \(m\) reactants, you don’t get \(m\)-body interaction, but instead \(m-1\) pairwise interaction in sequence, each consuming the product of the previous step as one of its input. The full reaction is therefor much akin to a left-associative fold over the set of reactants if we are to speak in functional programming style (arguably much better computationally).
The constraint is similar to how Boolean binary algebra works, of the nested constraint in between the chemical components. This means of the implication that the order of interaction matters, for which pair to be consumed in such as the first implication. Second, it also means that for interaction specificity, we can also switch the order of which if I bracket \(N_{34},N_{35}\) first, thereby the chain of order would spread out in between itself. Implicitly, we can quite also see what is happening with this composition. Under reaction in which \(N_{j}\) is the reactant to both \(N_{n}\) and \(N_{q}\), then there must be 2 separated chains, one concerns with \(N_{j}+N_{n}\) and the other with \(N_{j}+ N_{q}\), respectively. This incurs a rather costly debt of interpretation and chemical computation, as for them to be separated meaning now you will have to gauge and control the whole number separation between them. Under some circumstances (or rather most), such often cannot be obtained itself, or at least if you gauge them, you are also doing local radii reaction computation, which in turns will force the chemical formulation to be consistent as to have independent reactive elements, which the framework does not provide explanation to. The last mundane observation from such point, before we move on to the other postulates, would be that in local bracket, order of reaction in formulation does not matter. Which is partly true in practical chemistry, but with nuance we are not to explain here but refer to authoritative texts. In modern science, (Voelkel 2017) provided such view into the order of addition for chemical reaction itself, and (Bourne 2003) on mixing in chemical processes.
Moving on, atoms cannot be subdivided into smaller units, such is to say that they are unchanged and of a particular optimal baseline that cannot be crossed of the higher precision pointer. The implication is rather immediate if not. The atom by then, would be the main actor of every single chemical process itself, and would be favourable to capture their intrinsic properties and behaviours underlying the atomic reaction themselves. Because atoms are the same by postulate 2 of same size, mass and other properties, this creates a form of independent correlation or uniformity invariance between the two atoms together of the same element - they will act the same and be the same of properties, thus the chemical reaction at a certain fixture would be scalable by only analyzing the small set of chemical elements itself, and can be applied within homogeneous assumption of such in large set of masses and order of process. It also implicitly foregrounded the conservation of matter and energy, such is to say if under classical notion, \((m,E)\)-configuration as a pair of ‘mass’ that an atom has, then they would only be taken away from the prior to the latter post-process form, and thus both would be conserved - the energy would be of specific quantity and be unchanged, so for mass.
Postulate 5 is rather contradicting postulate 4, in a sense. During which a process of chemical reactions, atom to be combined, separated and rearrange, there exists the condition in which take a 3-set of elements, \(N_{1},N_{2},N_{3}\), we have as following, \[
\begin{matrix}
N_{1} + N_{2} + N_{3} \to N_{r1} + N_{r2} \\
(N_{1}+ N_{2}) \to N_{r12,1} + N_{r12,2} + N_{r12,3} \\
N_{1} + N_{2} + N_{3} \equiv N_{r12,1} + N_{r12,2} + N_{r12,3} + N_{3}
\end{matrix}
\] However, the collapse if there is, of the left-hand-side, cannot be considered carefully and quantitatively. Specifically speaking, it relies on how well we detect the residue of the chemical experimental results, for \(N_{r1} + N_{r2}\). Now, another possibility that will complicate this is where we have \[
\begin{matrix}
N_{1} + N_{2} + N_{3} \to N_{r1} + N_{r2} \\
(N_{2}+ N_{3}) \to N_{r23,1}  \\
N_{1} + N_{2} + N_{3} \equiv N_{r23,1} + N_{1}
\end{matrix}
\] in which the chain might collapse to one, or two variations that give the two reactant first. This route is much cleaner, but also is concerned of the same problem as the preceded formulation are. There exists no consistent analysis as to why such can happen, and how the collapse is guaranteed. This is a rather interesting entry point to what we know as transition state theory, reaction mechanism, and catalysis theory of which are developed to address such. The consequence, however, is that we do not know for sure what type of order matters, and what process would be dissimilar from which. While it is easy to say combine, separate and so on, the harder task is to ask how the reaction takes precedence. It gives prevalence to the control theory of chemical process, though at this stage much of that would be able within the framework, not much so of others. Another implication would be specific. After you produced \(N_{r1} + N_{r2}\), here comes the question. Suppose we have \[
N_{r1} + N_{r2} + N_{4} \to \: ?
\] How would you identify the mechanism again of \(N_{r1}\), for example, compound? Atomic specificity identifies dynamic under elements. However, compounds are much different. The combinatorial exponential explosion would be apparent from here, and such is opened for analysis. Suppose there exists \(0\geq k_{i}\geq K\) compound coefficient count. Then, for large interaction thereof, there exists \[
\# \text{ compounds} = (K+1)^{n} - 1
\] The exponential here being of the order \(n\). For \(n=4\), the distinctive compounds resolution is 80. Given \(m\) reactants, and only binary combination of the number of ways to parenthesise all \(N_{1} + N_{2} + N_{3} + \dots + N_{m}\), the number of ways would be hypothesized to be \[

\] in which reaction ordering increases substantially. The total stack gives us \((K+1)^{n}\times 4^{m}\) tracking reaction tree in plurality case of multi-reactant under ordering. This also again, imported the ordering specificity stated above that force the binary reaction being this way.

In a sense, the framework promised of the resolution to Act IV that matter/material could be understood through discrete combinatorial units in simple rational ratios. What the analysis reveals is that this promise generates a search space whose complexity grows faster than any systematic investigation procedure - empirical or computational - can handle, within the baseline of the growth that would be too expensive to attack. The framework is not just incomplete, since its postulate would be rather intuitively sensible even of the current time. However, unfortunately, it is computationally intractable as a theory of material identity for any system of realistic complexity.

Under chemical compound, there exists the question of how to track them, specifically, of which is \(X=A+B\), for \(k_1 = k_2 = 1\), then the new compound \(N_{\mathrm{new}}\) is not decidable internally. Both satisfies fixed composition, reproducible properties, conserved mass up to observation heuristics, of which there exists no other way to classify them altogether. The move is then to have two incompatible reaction space to \(X+C\) of the third element. Either primitive-\(X\) where you treat it as \(X\) to \(C\), or compossibility of interaction to get the full-chain consistency, but you don’t really know the post-local compound of how it will work with \(C\), and hence have to rely on again, specific auditing process of a full book-length table lookup on every possible compound combination. Again, suppose the same setting. For compound interaction, you require \(r:(X,Y)\mapsto P\) of products, where \(X,Y\) can be elements or compounds. Essentially, this is a function on two space of the \[
r: (\mathcal{N}\times \mathcal{C}) \times (\mathcal{N}\times \mathcal{C}) \to \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})
\] of the pair \((\mathcal{N}\times \mathcal{C})\) on element-count scheme. The size of the lookup table would be, approximately on \(O(\exp)\), to be around \[
S = m+M \approx (K+1)^{m}, \quad S^{2} \sim (K+1)^{2m}
\] for \(m\) elements, \(M\) distinct compound. Each compound has two modes, either primitive of the \(N_{\mathrm{new}}\) component, or decomposable to \(k_1,...,k_m\). Then, we have \[

\] Thus, the total complexity now would be of the order in exponential class, plus what has been known before of the pathway dependency. Now, since the baseline shift of the lookup table is included, the complexity is instead of, \[
\mathsf{Comp} \sim (K+1)^{2m} \times 2^{(K+1)^{m}} \times 4^{K}.
\] This is a super-exponential classification table on itself, which again, is very hard to compute. Without much to say about later discovery of isotope and many inexplainable kinematic variations, Dalton’s theory itself is simply large to the point of undecidable given the scale itself. Isotope proves that something underneath the atomic model gives us different mass profile for the same configuration of other properties, while nuclear fission of radioactive compounds provides evidence that atom can be again decomposed. Within such, the next elaboration is simple, to see the lower-order of the atomic structure itself. But how?



3.2.2 Cracking the barriers
The 89 years of which will follow to Dalton from Thomson (the pudding) is very structurally interesting, and it underlies the current landscape itself of what there are of the tension between theoretical notions, and the practical layering that makes up the bulk of it. Analytically speaking, it is the sequence of four distinct crises, each of which put pressure on the Daltonian framework from a different question, systematically revealing that the postulates are hiding something underneath, for example, the atomic specificity of non-destruction. Each of which the framework would survive by deferral rather than resolution, which cumulatively being the weakening effect of the programme. Often, we jumped simply from Dalton to Thomson without much thought about what constitutes in between, though history would be said otherwise - the surprise is not without warning, but the resolution of a tension that had been building for nearly a century, and of which, all without impulse, led to Rutherford’s.

Prout’s hypothesis and the atomic weight problem (1815–1860s)
Approximately seven years after Dalton, William Prout published paper sin 1815 and 1816 observing that the atomic weights of the known elements appeared to be whole multiples of the atomic weight of hydrogen, hypothesizing that the hydrogen atom was the only true fundamental object and that atoms of other element were the grouping of hydrogen atoms. The prime matter now returned with the flawed model of such, as we found out, but now supported by empirical patterns that would seem to say validate the experiment and hypothesis. But so are many prime matter theory coming before it on itself. Nevertheless, it can be regarded as the prime matter crack of the lower-level concern for the Daltonian framework. Prout is asking Act IV, internally within Dalton’s own frameworks. Specifically speaking, Dalton presupposed the atomic species. However, Prout hypothesized that it is not indeed the atomic species but simply different variations of the hydrogen atoms that made up the world on and by itself, thus the model of atomic structure is instead hydrogen-base, atomically composite of hydrogen atoms instead.
The action itself is not wrong. Indeed, when we consider the hydrogen atom, it can be said to be the simplest ever atom observed of the physical reality with its configurations. Implicitly, the Daltonian framework does not reject Prout’s hypothesis, but simply just giving a justification of compositions for where all the atomic differentiation between different atomic species are from, in the form being the answer as modularity, where the simplest structure helps itself to create a newer theory.
Let us deploy the hypothesis. Suppose that we have the set of \(\mathcal{N}\equiv\{N\}\) chemical elements. Then, Daltonian framework says that they differ three fundamental categories. First, mass \(m\), second, size \(v\) if we are to speak of volumetric adherence, and third, \(p_{1},...,p_{n}\) of certain other properties. Because of the aforementioned compound problem, we suppose the properties list would be complexity-dependent that would emerge inconsistently and fundamentally plural given its circumstances and setup of the empirical usages. Then, we focus on \(m\) and \(v\). Because \(v\) as we now know, is approximately small on the order of \(\mu m\), by Daltonian scale, they can be said to approximately negligible as the choice of comparison. Then, the question remains would be to distinguish one singular element from another. This pushes the question to the atom itself as to ask what is the atom? More specifically, can there be existence of the simplest possible atom that would explain for how it was formed? That is Prout’s direction. The other direction would be the anti-modularity formalists in the sense of non-collapse into atom composition, but to say that in general, the atoms differ like balloon - some can be big, some can be small, but they are configured that way and of the same concentration mechanics. This foregrounds the extrapolation outside the framework, implicitly, but internally of Daltonian framework, such allows for saying of the special element \(N\) from \(M\), thus validates Daltonian than being extracted of the implication. Daltonian modularity search comes with a problem. How do you presuppose the singular atom? There are many choices for that. For example, \(\mathrm{He}\) for helium is with currently specified atomic mass to be around \(4.002602\). By the time of Daltonian precision, that equates to simply \(4\). Oxygen is \(15.9994\), approximately still to be \(16\). Then, indeed, we can say that helium constitutes oxygen. Which is weird, because Helium cannot form Nitrogen or Boron because of the whole number requirement. Lithium (for \(\mathrm{Li}\) to be \(\sim 6.941\)) would be close to forming Neon, as \(\mathrm{Ne}\sim 20.1797\). The pattern is inconsistent, but it is rather clear from experiments, they are non-trivially large. The only candidate that would be feasible under such thinking of such, without asking the blocked move of what is even the atom, would be to take hydrogen, which is of approximately \(1.00794\) atomic mass. The number is almost too nice, and for the precision of the time, such can be said to simple one. That is where Prout was, and how the conjecture was formed. Surprisingly however, the issue is self-referential, using its own assumptions to immunize itself against the question those assumptions generated, of which would be seen in its response against Prout.
The Daltonian framework, by then, responded by rejecting Prout empirically. A series of more careful measurements of the atomic weights, compiled by Berzelius in 1828 and Turner in 1832, disproved quite so of the hypothesis - in particular of the atomic weight of chlorine, the proportion is \(35.45\) instead, which is not whole number as said. In fact, Berzelius, the foremost analytical chemist that compiled such, said in his work to be:

This work belongs to those few productions from which science will derive no advantage whatever […] The greatest civility which his contemporaries can show the author, is to forget that it was ever published.

Ironically, however, the result of being \(35.45\) times that of Hydrogen worked against his favour, of which would be our current atomic model of current time. Suppose that the process we have contains a chemical reaction, specifically, between chlorine, oxygen, and hydrogen. The Thomson’s paper - On the Structure of the Atom
Let us trace his paper from the start. It begins as to state of the central problem of the time - the view that “the atoms of elements consist of a number of negatively electrified (charged) corpuscles enclosed in a sphere of uniform positive electrification”, of which suggest a configuration where \(n\) negatively electrified, or so electron, corpuscles are probed of their motions inside such system. What he was hinting at, is toward the existence of particles, thus posit that the configuration of the system from his knowledge and of the time, to be in equilibrium. Such is why the problem starts with equilibrium structure situation, and continue on with motions inside this equilibrium sphere. We note that under this view, none of the \(e_{n}\) escapes the structure of the atom itself.
For charge \(ve\) of the sphere, \(b\) sphere radius and \(a\) radius of the corpuscle, then \[
G_{corp}= \frac{ve^{2}a}{b^{3}}, \quad G_{ij} = \frac{e^{2}}{4r_{i}^{2}\sin{(1/2)\theta_{ij}}}
\] is the positive electrification force attracting the corpuscle; here, \(\theta_{ij}\) is the angle made by the joint \(r_{i}\) and \(r_{j}\), of two objects \(A\) and \(B\) of such distance from the centre of the sphere. This presupposes radially uniform, single directed attractive force toward the corpuscle, even inside the positive sphere. Surprisingly, yet rather interesting, this also conditions a point-attractive valley, or an atom. The other forces in action, is the repulsion \(G_{ij}\), of which for uniform distribution of \(2\pi/n\) on a single ring, then the radial repulsion on one corpuscle due to the other \((n-1)\) is equal to \[
\frac{e^{2}}{4a^{2}} \left( \csc{\frac{\pi}{n}} + \csc{\frac{2\pi}{n}} + \csc{\frac{3\pi}{n}} + \dots + \csc{\frac{(n-1)\pi}{n}} \right)
\] The radial attraction, \(G_{corp}=S_{n}\) for \(n\) corpuscles, in equilibrium position, must equal to such expression, hence, \[
S_{n}= \frac{e^{2}}{4a^{2}} \left( \csc{\frac{\pi}{n}} + \csc{\frac{2\pi}{n}} + \csc{\frac{3\pi}{n}} + \dots + \csc{\frac{(n-1)\pi}{n}} \right) \equiv \frac{e^{2}}{4a^{2}} \sum^{n}_{i=2}\csc{\frac{(i-1)\pi}{i}}
\] or, in a simplified form, \[
\frac{a^{3}}{b^{3}} = \frac{S_{n}}{4v}
\] The separated values are computed explicitly with both \(S_{n}\) and \(a/b\), using empirical predictions of the time. If the ring of the corpuscles, instead of being at rest, is rotating with an angular velocity \(\omega\), the condition for steady motion is \[
\frac{ve^{2}a}{b^{3}} = ma\omega^{2} + \frac{e^{2}}{4a^{2}} S_{n}
\] or with manipulation algebraically, \[
\frac{va^{3}}{b^{3}} = \frac{m}{e^{2}}\omega^{2} + \frac{S_{n}}{4}
\] here \(m\) is the mass of a corpuscle. In the subsequent phases, after dealing with equilibrium state, what would happen is the argument when the corpuscles are slightly displaced from their positions equilibrium. Let the position of the corpuscles be fixed by the polar coordinates \(r\) and \(\theta\) in the plane of the undisturbed orbit, by displacement \(z\) at right angles to this plane. Let \(r_{s},\theta_{s},z_{s}\) be the coordinates of the \(s\)-th corpuscle. The slight disturbance from their positions can be said to be \(r_{s}=a+\rho_{s}\) where \(\rho_{s}\)is small compared with \(a\), \(z_{s}\) is also small compared with \(a\), and \(\theta_{s}-\theta_{s-1}=2\pi/n + \phi_{s}-\phi_{s-1}\), where \(n\) is the number of corpuscles and \(\phi\)’s are small quantities of the same form on perturbation mechanics. The intention is to see if the condition can be reverted of equilibrium from the radial repulsion, which encapsulates the system by description to stabilize the atom. For such, the radial repulsion exerted by the \(s\)-th corpuscle on the \(p\)-th is equal to \[
-e^{2} \frac{d}{dr_{p}} \frac{1}{(r^{2}_{p}+r_{s}^{2}-2r_{p}r_{s}\cos{(\theta_{s}-\theta_{p})}+(z_{p}-z_{s})^{2})^{1/2}}
\] For this, solving and deriving, he obtains the equation of motion of the \(p\)-th corpuscle under that constrained and perturbation, given as \[
\begin{align*}
    & m \left(\frac{d^{2}r_{p}}{dt^{2}}-r_{p} \left(\frac{d\theta_{p}}{dt}\right)^{2} \right) = -\frac{ve^{2}r_{p}}{b^{3}}+ R_{p}; \\
    & m \left( r \frac{d^{2}\theta_{p}}{dt^{2}} + 2\frac{dr}{dt} \frac{d\theta_{p}}{dt} \right) = \Theta_{p} \\
    & m \frac{d^{2}z_{p}}{dt^{2}} = -\frac{ve^{2}}{b^{3}}z_{p} + Z_{p}
\end{align*}
\] for individual radial, tangential and right angle forces, respectively. Solving this using frequency theory of the time, he obtains the frequency equation as \[
\left( \frac{3}{4} \frac{e^{2}}{a^{3}} S + L_{k} - L_{0} - mq^{2} \right) (N_{0}-N_{k}-mq^{2}) = (M_{k} - 2m\omega q)^{2}
\] for \(k\) in this equation varies of order from \(0\) to \((n-1)\). The notation is defined in the document, of which would be rather interested if you are to see from the paper itself (a copy can be found here, respectively). By a series of derivation, solving and targeting the right angles motion, the problem is reduced to the expression for the descriptive dynamics as \[
\frac{ve}{b^3} + P_{k} - P_{0} - mq^{2} = 0
\] Putting in succession \(k=0,1,...,n-1\), we can get \(n\) values of \(q\) giving the \(n\) frequencies corresponding to the displacements at right angles to the plane of the undisturbed orbit. To then calculate the frequencies for systems containing various numbers of corpuscles, the four quantities specified above, namely \(L_k, M_k, N_k, P_k\) which occurs in the frequency equation, can now be completely computed by \[
\begin{align*}
    T_{k} & = \sum^{n-1}_{1}\cos{\frac{2\pi ks}{n}} \left( \sin^{3}{\frac{s\pi}{n}}\right)^{-1} \\
    S_{k} & = \sum^{n-1}_{1}\cos{\frac{2\pi ks}{n}} \left( \sin{\frac{s\pi}{n}}\right)^{-1} \\
    U_{k} & = \sum^{n-1}_{1}\sin{\frac{2\pi ks}{n}} \left( \dfrac{\cos{\dfrac{s\pi}{n}}}{\sin^{2}{\dfrac{s\pi}{n}}}\right)
\end{align*}
\] which gives \[
\begin{matrix}
    L_{k} (S_{k}+T_{k}) \dfrac{e^{2}}{8a^{3}} & N_{k} = (2T_{k} - S_{k}) \dfrac{e^{2}}{8a^{3}} \\
    M_{k} = U_{k} \dfrac{e^{2}}{8a^{3}} & P_{k} = T_{k} \dfrac{e^{2}}{8a^{3}}
\end{matrix}
\] This can be then used, in the paper, to solve for case of two corpuscles, i.e. \(n=2\) up to \(n=6\). Interestingly, the model predicts instability at \(n\geq 7\) and so on, particularly requiring stability analysis of sort. Indeed, “for a single corpuscle in the centre is sufficient to make rings of 7 and 8 corpuscles stable”, thence given such, there exists an extreme minimal on which a single electron repulse and operate on the dual purpose - both being electronic configuration of the system, both providing repulsive stabilisation force. When the number of corpuscles exceeds 8, however, “the number of central corpuscles required to ensure stability increases very rapidly with the number of corpuscles in the ring”. The frequency equation, that is, \[
\left(\frac{3 e^{2} S_{0}}{4 a^{3}}+ \frac{3 p e^{2}}{a^{3}}- \left(L_{0} - L_{k}\right)- m q^{2}\right)\left(N_{0} - N_{k} - m q^{2}\right)=\left(M_{k} - 2 m \omega q\right)^{2}.
\] gives the least condition, that is, \[
\frac{3pe^{2}}{a^{3}} > (L_{0}-L_{n/2}) - \frac{3}{4} \frac{e^{2}S_{0}}{a^{3}}, \quad \frac{3pe^{2}}{a^{3}} > (L_{0}-L_{(n-1)/2}) - \frac{3}{4} \frac{e^{2}S_{0}}{a^{3}}
\] Here, \(p\) is the number of stabilization electrons, or as stated of the paper, internal corpuscles. Indeed, within such, we can see the pattern as shown in the calculation of Thomson:

Electronic stability - Larmor energy drain
Larmor in his Aether and Matter of the 1900, gave the energy lost by which Maxwellian electrodynamics predicted of radiation energy from accelerating (of the time, note that relativistic effect is still not quite a thing), which would leave to an atomic collapse, of charge \(e\) revolving with speed \(v\) on a circle of radius \(a\), as \[
\frac{dE}{dt} = \frac{2}{3} \left( \frac{e^{2}v^{4}}{ca^{2}} \right)
\] for here \(c\) denotes the velocity of light. For most electronic configuration with many electrons, the effect will not be so additive. On the contrary, considering the case \(n\) electron, Thomson proved that the radiation drain reduced drastically with \(n\) with specific configuration, though this comes with a cost of non-uniformity in analysis. The general formulation of energy lost is given by, under \(n\)-equidistantly placed configuration of electrons on a single ring, the derivation gives \[
\left( \frac{dE}{dt} \right)_{n} = \frac{2ce^2 \beta^{2n+2}}{a^{2}} \frac{(n+1)n^{2n+3}}{(2n+1)!}
\] where \(\beta=v/c\) was assumed to be small. However, the issue is much more deliberate, moreso as to be serious in its form. In his original paper on the topic, derivation for stability states of \(n=6\) was made, but a ring of 7-8 corpuscle can also be obtained per generality. it is also from here we come to the true shape of how electron are configured, not just a single ring, but multiple, coming from top to bottom and together form a cloud, which, ironically, is similar to current modern physics. The frequency equation that he used to solve on stability condition for seven or eight corpuscles, comes off as (recited from above) \[
\left(\frac{3 e^{2} S_{0}}{4 a^{3}}+ \frac{3 p e^{2}}{a^{3}}- \left(L_{0} - L_{k}\right)- m q^{2}\right)\left(N_{0} - N_{k} - m q^{2}\right)=\left(M_{k} - 2 m \omega q\right)^{2}.
\] For the condition equal, the meaning of such equation inferred into the normal framework is basically a frequency normal-mode equation for small oscillation of \(n\) electron, under configuration of multi-layering ring inside the usual ‘fluid’ uniform positive sphere. title: 6  Reviewing the scripts
text:
Schematic overview of the requirements for an effective structural representation. The mapping between structures and feature space should obey fundamental physical symmetries (equivalent structures should be mapped to the same features), should be complete (inequivalent structures should be mapped to distinct features), and should be smooth (continuous deformations of a structure should map to a smooth deformation of the associated features). Furthermore, whenever dealing with datasets that are not homogeneous in molecular size, the representation should be additive: a structure should be decomposed in a sum of local environments (usually atom-centered), ensuring transferability and extensivity of predictions.
